title: Handley Page Halifax JB863
memorial_details:
Black, rectangular, marble tablet mounted at a low, oblique angle on a low, brick-built plinth. The dedication is in gold, raised, upper and lower-case letters. A picture of a Halifax bomber is top centre of the tablet.

The memorial is erected by the community of Elvington, indicating a strong local connection.

The inscription was erected by the community of Elvington, the crew's home station.
inscription: TO THE MEMORY OF/ (names)/ MEMBERS OF 77 SQUADRON FROM ELVINGTON WHO LOST THEIR/ LIVES IN A HALIFAX BOMBER WHICH CRASHED NEAR THIS SITE/ DURING TAKEOFF ON A BOMBING MISSION TO LE CRUESOT FRANCE/ 10.06 PM 19TH JUNE 1943/ THEY GAVE THEIR TODAY FOR OUR TOMORROW

sources.title: Facebook post by Daran Walker (RAF Bomber Command Memorials group)

narrative: Halifax JB863 (KN-V) of 77 Squadron, based at RAF Elvington, crashed shortly after take-off on the evening of 19 June 1943 while bound for Le Creusot, France. The aircraft came down on what is now the course of Fulford Golf Club near Heslington, York. Several airmen were killed. The memorial tablet is maintained by Fulford Golf Club.
community_connection: The memorial is maintained by Fulford Golf Club, whose course occupies ground close to the crash site.
crew_note: Names on memorial not transcribed in inscription source (IWM). 7 names appear on the physical tablet.
